merged.title: feat(sdk): hero steering and movement, effect quads, sparks and the Thruster-Pack flame as hook points
merged.author: Promises
merged.untrustedBody:
## What

Five new rac1 hook points for mods:

- **`rac1.player.steer_planar_velocity`** (`Hero_SteerPlanarVelocity`, `void(f32)`, param `step`): `steer_hero_planar_velocity`, which steers the hero's planar velocity toward his target speed. One hook point over the function (levels 0, 4, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 17) and its copy `air_accel` (the other ten levels).
- **`rac1.player.update_movement`** (`Hero_UpdateMovement`, `void()`): the hero's movement for his current state, called once a tick from `Hero_UpdateMotionInput`. One hook point over 14 copies: `hero_update_movement` (levels 0, 4, 7, 9, 10, 13) and each other level's own copy of it.
- **`rac1.fx.world_quad.draw`** (`FX_DrawWorldQuad`, `void(u32,u32,i32)`, params `quad`, `matrix`, `mode`): `draw_world_quad`, the effect quad routine that most effects' draw callbacks call. merged.title: fix(rac1): relocate current_vu_chain and space_load_in_progress in space transitions
merged.author: Clank700
merged.untrustedBody:
Fixes the crash `read at game address 0x50000010` (`func_001F9A98 <- space.c:2425`) that shows up after **Load** from the start menu and when travelling by ship, roughly one try in three or four. It also removes the `unusable camera (eye 1.5845633e+29 ...)` warnings logged every 96 ticks in every loading-scene mode.

## Cause

`initialize_level_runtime` in `space.c` reaches two globals by adding a byte offset to unrelated ones:

- `current_vu_chain_r` is `&D_00160000 + 0x100C` (meant: `D_0016100C`)
- `space_load_in_progress_r` is `&D_0015F560 + 0x19C` (meant: `D_0015F6FC`)

Hostgen turns them into `OPENRAC_DATA(0x00160000u) + 0x100C` and `OPENRAC_DATA(0x0015F560u) + 0x19C`. On the boot transition (no level overlay) the sums land on the right words. On every later transition a level overlay is loaded and these globals relocate by different amounts, so the two writes hit unrelated level data and `current_vu_chain` keeps the previous level's value (`0x60000` on Kalebo III, not `0x100000`)

merged.title: fix(runtime): an executable global between two pairs that moved alike moves with them
merged.author: farfeduc
merged.untrustedBody:
`relocate()` turns an executable global into its address in the loaded level, using the pairs its functions' code gives. An address that no pair is near (within 0x100 below it) and no code forms was kept as it was.

RAC1's pause screens (0x001CEA80 on NTSC-U) are such an address: the game reaches them through a pointer. In a level they stayed at the executable's address, where other data lies, so a mod writing there through `relocate()` corrupted the level's data.

## The fix

When the nearest pairs below and above such an address moved by the same amount, the data between them moved as one block, and the address now moves with them. In level 1, 0x1CE798 and 0x1CEC20 both moved by -0x1BA80, so the pause screens are at 0x1B3000.

Between pairs that moved apart, nothing says where the data went, and the address is kept as before. `OPENRAC_TRACE_RELOCATION` names the pairs around each such address.

merged.title: fix(hostgen): pass a record over eight bytes by address where a pointer is taken
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
Going Commando PAL crashed in the Protopet fight on Yeedil (phase 2). `trooper_init_spawned` (PAL C) passes a 12-byte struct of three links by value to `moby_fuse_linked_objects`, which takes a pointer. hostgen passed the struct's first word, a moby address, so the callee read garbage pointers (crash report: read at game address 0x483AEAB2).

## After
The troopers spawn and the fight goes on.

## How
The EE's ABI (EABI) passes a record bigger than eight bytes as the address of a copy. hostgen now does the same: it copies the record into a frame slot and passes its address. Records of eight bytes or less still go in the register, and their frames keep their size. The decomp C is not changed.

## Tested
- New hostgen test (fails before, passes after); test_hostgen, test_release, test_release_rac2 pass.
- Generated C diffed for rac2 PAL/NTSC, rac1 PAL/NTSC and rac3: only the PAL Yeedil call changes behaviour.
- Not tested in game (no PAL disc in the container).

merged.title: perf(hostgen): one Clang run per read and a parallel prepared copy
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
hostgen ran Clang twice for each read of a unit: a syntax check, then the AST dump. The prepared copy of the decompilation was made on one core. The 7 game versions took 23.5 min of hostgen on 4 cores, most of the CI "Build the game" step.

## After
One Clang run per read: the AST dump reports the same errors. The prepared copy is made in hostgen's worker processes. The 7 versions take 14.9 min (-37%).

| version | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| rac2-pal | 448 s | 248 s |
| rac2-ntsc2 | 320 s | 199 s |
| rac2-ntsc | 266 s | 161 s |
| other 4 | 377 s | 283 s |

## Tested
- Generated C of all 7 versions is byte for byte the same as before (`diff -rq`).
- `python -m unittest discover -s port/tools/hostgen`: 318 tests pass.
- Not run: a CI build on this branch.

merged.title: fix(rac2-pal): call the level's helpers from the levels' Spider Bot
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** In PAL, the game crashed when the Spider Bot blew up in Todano ("read at game address 0x3D23D772"). The levels' Spider Bot C uses the same `ref_L00_003DD6A8_*` names as the executable's copy, so the PAL release table sent three of its calls to executable functions. `moby_set_linked_flag` then read its pointer at 0x001AF8F0, which holds a float (0.04) in Todano.

merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
A load or store that runs past the last byte of main memory or of the scratchpad read and wrote past the host mapping, so the interpreter died with a bus error. rac3's functional gate hit it with made-up calls (`fcheck --fuzz`), where a pointer can land on the last bytes of RAM.

Such an access is one the console refuses (it is already counted as misaligned). It now goes a byte at a time: the bytes inside memory go to memory, and those past main memory go to the hardware callbacks. Aligned accesses take the same path as before.

The interpreter is a test-only tool (fcheck, captures); nothing in the port or the launcher uses it.

merged.title: fix(rac2): decompress game WAD streams as the disc routine does
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Fixes T-77.

**Before:** on Damosel, the map screen could crash with "Going Commando WAD decompression failed" (a literal runs past the end of the stream). The map cache can glue one map's header onto another map's body; this is game logic and happens on the original too.

**After:** the game reads such a stream like the original and carries on.

opened.title: fix(hostgen): pass a record over eight bytes by address where a pointer is taken
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
## Before
Going Commando PAL crashed in the Protopet fight on Yeedil (phase 2). `trooper_init_spawned` (PAL C) passes a 12-byte struct of three links by value to `moby_fuse_linked_objects`, which takes a pointer. hostgen passed the struct's first word, a moby address, so the callee read garbage pointers (crash report: read at game address 0x483AEAB2).

## After
The troopers spawn and the fight goes on.

## How
The EE's ABI (EABI) passes a record bigger than eight bytes as the address of a copy. hostgen now does the same: it copies the record into a frame slot and passes its address. Records of eight bytes or less still go in the register, and their frames keep their size. The decomp C is not changed.

## Tested
- New hostgen test (fails before, passes after); test_hostgen, test_release, test_release_rac2 pass.

opened.title: fix(interpreter): a misaligned access at the end of memory stays in what is mapped
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
A load or store that runs past the last byte of main memory or of the scratchpad read and wrote past the host mapping, so the interpreter died with a bus error. rac3's functional gate hit it with made-up calls (`fcheck --fuzz`), where a pointer can land on the last bytes of RAM.

Such an access is one the console refuses (it is already counted as misaligned). It now goes a byte at a time: the bytes inside memory go to memory, and those past main memory go to the hardware callbacks. Aligned accesses take the same path as before.

The interpreter is a test-only tool (fcheck, captures); nothing in the port or the launcher uses it.

Test: `openrac-ps2-tests` has a new case, "access at the end of memory", and all 298 checks pass.

opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
Before: the Windows launcher build failed while building Embree for the probe baker. Embree adds -std=c++11, and Visual Studio's C++ library (MSVC 14.52) does not compile as C++11.

After: Embree is built as C++14 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=14, no extensions). CMake puts its flag after Embree's, so it wins.

opened.title: fix(rac2): decompress game WAD streams as the disc routine does
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
Fixes T-77.

**Before:** on Damosel, the map screen could crash with "Going Commando WAD decompression failed" (a literal runs past the end of the stream). The map cache can glue one map's header onto another map's body; this is game logic and happens on the original too.

**After:** the game reads such a stream like the original and carries on.

**How:** game calls to the decompressor (0x0029D4D0 and its PAL/v2 rows) use a new decoder that follows the disc routine: no end check inside a packet, pads skip to the next 0x2000 chunk, little literals always read 3 bytes. It only fails where the original traps (a literal packet right after literals) or reads off memory. Clean streams give the same bytes as before.

**Tested:** disc_wad unit test; NTSC-U Damosel map runs in the container: the T-77 error now survives, and every other in-game decompression gave the same output as the strict decoder.

opened.title: fix(build): link Embree with the DLL runtime on Windows
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
Before: on Windows the probe baker did not link. Embree was built with the static C runtime (/MT) and the baker with the DLL runtime (/MD): lld-link stopped on a RuntimeLibrary mismatch. Embree's compiler settings clear the release flags that carry the runtime choice.

After: on Windows, Embree is configured with policy CMP0091 on and CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreadedDLL, so it uses /MD like the port.

How: a Windows-only set of Embree options in tools/build_port.py. Android passes windows=False. The options are in Embree's stamp, so a cached Windows Embree is built again once.

Tested: tools tests pass, with a new test for the Windows options. Not run: the Windows job itself (no Windows here).

opened.title: Add 10 near misses that are exact only with inline asm (plzcw, blezl abs)
opened.author: farfeduc
opened.untrustedBody:
Ten main-image functions (each in 14 level places under the same name) compile to retail's bytes, but only with two inline asm helpers. CONTRIBUTING.md and `docs/agents/levers.md` do not allow inline asm in matched C, so they go to `nonmatching/` as near misses, not `src/`.

**Why inline asm**
- **plzcw** (leading sign bits, used as floor/ceil log2 of texture sizes): SN 2.95.3 has `__builtin_plzcw`, but it works on 128-bit values and adds `por` copies and a sign extension. No C form gives retail's bare `plzcw`. About 25 main-image functions use it.
- **abs written `blezl x; sub x, $0, x`**: GCC's abs is `bltzl` + `negu`, and no compiler in `toolchain/` has a `blezl` pattern. The disassembler already marks this `neg` as a handwritten instruction (func_00493888). About 10 functions use it.

So the original source had inline asm here. If maintainers want an exception for instructions the compiler cannot emit (for example one small header with the two helpers), these ten can move to `src/`

merged.title: fix: enemy copies, party host takeover and edge cases in Difficulty
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before: with Enemy count above 1, copies of path and cover enemies (Novalis birdbots, troopers, saw bots) stood on top of each other: they hid each other, caught each other's shots and split apart once hit. Spawned and big enemies could still overlap. When a party's host left, the new host ran no Chaos events or enemy copies, and an event on at that moment never ended.

After:
- Birdbots, mine layers and minibombers are no longer copied (their init puts them at their path's start).
- Copies keep apart from every enemy of their class: spawned ones too, big ones by their own size (up to 4 units). They never go through walls, and walking ones never go off ledges. The level's own enemies are never moved.
- A new host keeps the party's rules and runs the events and copies itself (Multiplayer hands the rules over to its mods; the Item Randomizer keeps the party's seed).
- Bolt counts are restored after Moby_RecordDeath, a health orb never lowers health, and a member no longer moves copies.
